sourceBaseline: cc2873b5 (pushed dev commit of Fast Checks run 40187427911)
originalFailure: Fast Checks run 40187427911, job 121151078654 'Agent Tools Shard 2' (ubuntu-latest x86_64, CPython 3.12.15): outcome failure after 0.0022 s. The shard step hit its 50-minute timeout before unittest printed tracebacks, so only the public per-test event below survives.
confirmedCause: The case unlinked disk.img and at once wrote a same-size replacement. A Linux filesystem reissues a just-freed inode number to the next inode it creates, so the replacement had the original's device, inode number, size, owner and mode and _disk_pin returned an equal pin: the final assertNotEqual is the only assertion a 2 ms run can fail. Darwin's APFS (the only host Tart runs on) never reissues an inode number, which is why the case passed locally. _disk_pin itself is unchanged: the production pin runs only on the macOS Tart host.
fix: The replacement is made while the original inode is still held open (as a running VM holds its disk), so no filesystem can reissue its number; the assertion reports platform and both stats on failure.
controlledRegression: agent_tools.tests.test_readiness_tart_registry_inode_reuse runs the original case of this whole beforeimage and of the current module while readiness_tart_registry.Path reports, for every inode _disk_pin observes, the lowest number not held by a still-allocated earlier inode (a name in the pinned file's directory or a descriptor of this process), which is the Linux reissue rule; everything else is the actual file. It asserts the number each of the case's three pins observed, in order (original, after the guest write, replacement). A host filesystem that itself reissues the freed number (ext4 on the Linux runner) hands the replacement the original's own key, which keeps the original's number, so the expectation is the same on every host; the host's own inode numbers are printed on failure.
failingEvidence: Unfixed: under the Linux numbering the beforeimage case fails its final assertNotEqual and the three pins observe numbers [1, 1, 1]: the replacement repeats the original's reissued number. On this Darwin host the rule reissues it (the host numbers stay distinct); with an ext4-style native reissue simulated (the host repeats the original's own inode number while that inode is unlinked and closed) the observed numbers are the same [1, 1, 1]. Natively on Darwin, without the rule, the beforeimage case passes.
passingEvidence: Fixed: natively, under the Linux numbering and under the simulated native reissue the case passes and the three pins observe [1, 1, 2]; guest writes keep the pin and the replacement, made while the original is held, changes it.
routineSuite: agent_tools.tests.test_readiness_tart_registry_inode_reuse runs in the affected agent-test stage of the managed pre-push tier and the Fast Checks agent shards whenever the selector reaches it, including changes to test_readiness_tart_registry.py, readiness_tart_registry.py, this beforeimage or this provenance.
nativeEvidenceLimit: Hosted-runner test-harness outcome only; no Tart VM, disk image or macOS host behavior is involved or claimed. The native reissue was only simulated on this Darwin host; the next Linux Fast Checks run confirms the fixed case and this regression against the runner's native filesystem.
